acceptance: The process or call stack that deleted dists.dss is identified and recorded (log or watch output path)
A forced reproduction of that cause fails before the fix and passes after
The tpch_sf001_data integrity assertion is unchanged
context: Failing log kept at ~/.cache/benchbox/crr/preflight-5cb-attempt1.log (local to the maintainer host).
description:
## Problem
`make pr-preflight` on the corpus rule branch head 5cbaa06aed (2026-11-27) ended with 1 error after 23,695 passed tests: the teardown of the session fixture `tpch_sf001_data` (tests/conftest.py, the final `assert _tree_digest(cached_dir) == generated`) found `dists.dss` missing from the cached TPC-H SF 0.01 folder. It was present when the fixture generated the data. The error surfaced at the teardown of tests/unit/workflows/test_workflow_trigger_events.py::test_valid_event_shapes_are_accepted[on2], which is only where session teardown ran.

The cache lives under the session's own `tmp_path_factory` directory, and the fixture's consumers only copy it (`copy_to`). No BenchBox code deletes `dists.dss` (`_stage_distributions` in benchbox/core/tpch/generator.py only copies it in), and the branch changes neither tests/conftest.py nor the generator. Four earlier preflights on nearly identical code passed, so the deletion is intermittent. One unconfirmed hypothesis: other pytest sessions on the same host rotate `/private/var/folders/.../pytest-of-<user>/` and remove files under a running session's base temp directory.

## Change
- Find the deleting code or process with evidence (for example an audit hook or a file-system watch on the cache folder during a full preflight-order run), then fix the cause where it is.
- If the cause is concurrent pytest temp rotation, give each session a private basetemp (or equivalent) through the repository's test entry points, not per test.

## Decision gates
- Do not weaken or remove the fixture's integrity assertion; it is what caught this.
- If the cause cannot be reproduced after a watched full run plus a forced concurrent-session attempt, record the evidence and stop.

## Verification rubric
- The evidence names the process or call stack that removed the file.
- After the fix, a forced reproduction (for example a concurrent session started during the run, if that is the cause) no longer removes the file.

## Guardrails
- Reproduce or measure before changing anything; record the command, log path and run id in the item context.
- Fix the root cause. Never skip, xfail, loosen a check or bound, or raise a timeout only to make a test or run pass; a timing or limit change needs measured evidence and owner approval.
- No rule, check, label or test may name a platform or a version matrix unless the item is about that platform.
- Never edit stored result files under results-data/ or CHANGELOG.md; user-facing changes add a changelog.d fragment.
- No explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check); make duplicate-check-delta stays at +0; reuse existing helpers.
- Heavy work only through make heavy-run after make heavy-status, with command, maximum run time and log path announced first. Never touch the lock or set BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK, BENCHBOX_HEAVY_ADMIT=force, BENCHBOX_HEAVY_WATCHDOG=off, or raise BENCHBOX_HEAVY_MEMORY_BUDGET_GIB. No live cloud runs.
- Work in a linked worktree; one pull request; run the local review before opening it; fix hosted-review findings. No stand-in approval unless the owner names the PR and head.
- Re-read paths and line numbers before editing and report drift instead of guessing.
- When a decision gate's stop condition is met, stop and report to the owner with the evidence; never substitute a different decision.
